Compute the squared differences between the center pixel's depth and its three neighbors: right $(i+1, j)$, bottom $(i, j+1)$, and diagonal $(i+1, j+1)$ [S2].

The claim states that the squared differences are computed between the center pixel's depth and its right, bottom, and diagonal neighbors. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly defines the depth smoothness loss L_D using the formula: Σ [ (D̂_θ(r_{ij}) - D̂_θ(r_{i+1,j}))^2 + (D̂_θ(r_{ij}) - D̂_θ(r_{i,j+1}))^2 + (D̂_θ(r_{ij}) - D̂_θ(r_{i+1,j+1}))^2 ]. In this formula, r_{ij} represents the center pixel, r_{i+1,j} is the right neighbor, r_{i,j+1} is the bottom neighbor, and r_{i+1,j+1} is the diagonal neighbor. The terms are squared differences of the depth values. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present and supported by the evidence.

This formula confirms that the calculation involves summing squared differences (which are differences) over the pixel indices $(i,j)$ within the patch and over the set of rays $R_r$. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
